 About this position 
Data scarcity is a major challenge for developing European sovereign foundation models, especially for low-resource languages where additional training data is inherently limited. A promising solution is cross-lingual transfer: training models on related languages can improve performance on a target language more effectively than adding more data from the target language itself. 
The recent ATLAS study (Longpre et al. , 2025) is the largest empirical investigation of this effect to date, training 774 multilingual models across 50 languages and introducing the Bilingual Transfer Score (BTS) to measure how much one language benefits another. The study found that shared language family and script are the strongest predictors of transfer effectiveness. 
However, Dutch was not included in the ATLAS language set. This creates both a scientific and practical gap. ATLAS's predictors cannot distinguish whether English or German should be a better source language for Dutch, as both are Germanic languages written in the Latin script.
